{{short description|Danish physicist (born 1940)}}
{{sources|date=November 2014}}

'''Bjarne Tromborg''' (born 1940) was a [[Denmark|Danish]] [[physicist]], best known for his work in [[particle physics]] and [[photonics]].<ref name=ing>Henrik Skov, "Kernefysikeren der blev opslugt af optik", ''Ingeniøren'', Nov 27, 2005, http://ing.dk/artikel/67283-kernefysikeren-der-blev-opslugt-af-optik {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120210033800/http://ing.dk/artikel/67283-kernefysikeren-der-blev-opslugt-af-optik |date=2012-02-10 }}</ref> Bjarne died on June 11th 2025<ref>https://www.altinget.dk/person/bjarne-tromborg</ref> after a brief illness.{{citation needed|date=September 2025}} He is survived by his beloved wife, Ellen Marie, his daughter Marianne, and their grandchildren Natasha, Silvia, and Emilia.

==Biography==
{{unsourced section|date=November 2014}}
Tromborg was born in [[Give, Denmark|Give]], [[Denmark]]. In 1968, he received the M.Sc. degree in [[physics]] and [[mathematics]] from the [[Niels Bohr Institute]], in [[Copenhagen, Denmark]].  He was a university researcher studying high-energy [[particle physics]] from 1968 to 1978. In 1979, he joined the research laboratory of the Danish Teleadministrations in Copenhagen. He was Head of Optical Communications Department at Tele Danmark Research, [[Horsholm|Horsholm, Denmark]] from 1987 to 1995.

He was an adjunct professor at the [[Niels Bohr Institute]] from 1991 to 2001. In 1997, he took a leave of absence at the [[Technion - Israel Institute of Technology]]. Until his retirement at the end June 2006, he was a research professor at COM•DTU, Department of Communications, Optics and Materials (which became [[DTU Fotonik, Department of Photonics Engineering]], in 2008 and DTU Electro, Department of Electrical and Photonics Engineering, in 2022), [[Technical University of Denmark]].<ref>"Biografi Bjarne Tromborg", Ingenioren, November 27, 2005, {{cite web|url=https://ing.dk/artikel/bjarne-tromborg-67287 |accessdate=March 2, 2019 |title=Bjarne Tromborg |date=27 November 2005 }}</ref>

==Research==
{{unsourced section|date=November 2014}}
Tromborg co-authored a research [[monograph]] and approximately one hundred journal and conference publications, mostly on physics and [[optoelectronics]].

At the Niels Bohr Institute, he carried out research in [[elementary particle physics]], particularly analytic [[S-matrix theory]] and electromagnetic corrections to [[hadron]] scattering. He coauthored a research monograph on [[dispersion (optics)|dispersion]] theory.

In the early 1980s, he switched to [[photonics]]. Tromborg was one of the first to develop advanced theoretical models for complex [[semiconductor laser]] structures such as external [[Optical cavity|laser cavities]] and [[distributed feedback laser]]s in the beginning of the 1980s. Computer simulations and measurements confirmed the validity of the theoretical models and their predictions. Several co-workers including Henning Olesen, Gunnar Jacobsen, Jens Henrik Osmundsen, Finn Mogensen, Kristian Stubkjær, Jesper Mørk, Xing Pan, Hans Erik Lassen and [[Björn Jónsson]] contributed to this work over a period of almost 15 years until 1995.

At TeleDanmark Research in the late 1980s and early 1990s Tromborg and colleagues worked to study the dynamics of active [[semiconductor materials]] in order to understand the physical relaxation processes at play, their strength and characteristic time scales. A pump-probe set-up employing [[femtosecond laser]]s was established and modeling efforts were initialized. Tromborg led the effort to identify this as a topic that would remain important for many years and argued that Denmark should work to lead in the field. He also proposed theoretical methods that could be used to estimate the size of these [[ultrafast]] dynamical effects and their role in understanding the origin of nonlinear gain suppression in semiconductor lasers.

From 1999 to his retirement at the end of June 2006, Tromborg was with the Department of Communications, Optics and Materials ([[COM*DTU]]) at the Technical University of Denmark. In this period, he worked in both research and education, as well as in securing several [[European Union]] research projects for COM*DTU. Tromborg took up the field of [[photonic crystal]]s and initiated and contributed himself to activities within the theory of photonic crystals. He also applied general techniques within [[Stochastic process|stochastic]] theory and [[signal analysis]] to develop improved descriptions of noise spectra in nonlinear [[semiconductor optical amplifier]]s.

==Awards and recognition==
Tromborg received the Electro-prize from the [[Danish Society of Engineers]] in 1981.{{citation needed|date=November 2014}}

He was chairman of the [http://www.dops.dk/ Danish Optical Society] from 1999 to 2002.<ref>"News from ICO Members Worldwide", ICO Newsletter, April 2000, No. 43, {{cite web|url=http://www.ico-optics.org/ico_apr00.html |accessdate=April 12, 2012 |url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110912032650/http://www.ico-optics.org/ico_apr00.html |archivedate=September 12, 2011 |title=ICO Newsletter April 2000 }}</ref>

He was associate editor of the ''[[IEEE Journal of Quantum Electronics]]'' beginning in 2003.

At his retirement, a [[Academic conference|symposium]] on [[photonics]] was held in his honor on 22 June 2006 at the Technical University of Denmark.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dops.dk/pictures/pdf/bt_invitation.pdf |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2007-12-24 |url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071009185059/http://www.dops.dk/pictures/pdf/bt_invitation.pdf |archivedate=2007-10-09 }}</ref>
